newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf Air expects $60m from leased planes.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air expects $60m from leased planes.

text.p: Gulf Air's president said in remarks published on Thursday that the loss-making carrier expects to make $60 million a year from leasing aircraft.

Sheikh Ahmad bin Seif al-Nahayan told the London-based al-Hayat newspaper that Gulf Air had leased five of its aircraft this year to Philippine Airlines, Polish national air carrier LOT, EgyptAir and Ethiopian Airlines.
He said Gulf Air, which now has 32 aircraft, intends to lease out another two planes before the end of the year to help it return to profit.
Bahrain-based Gulf Air, owned by Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates state of Abu Dhabi, made a $159 million loss in 1995.
